output_text:
name: python-observability
description: Python structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing, and production debugging.

Use for logging, metrics, tracing, correlation IDs, dashboards, and production issues. Make logs machine-readable so teams can investigate without deploying code.

- Production logs: JSON via `structlog` (`structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso")`, `structlog.processors.JSONRenderer()`, `structlog.get_logger()`); use human-readable output locally. Include consistent fields for filtering and correlation.
- Use `structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars`, `structlog.processors.add_log_level`, `structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer`, and `structlog.processors.format_exc_info`. Use levels consistently: `DEBUG` diagnostics, `INFO` lifecycle/operations, `WARNING` recoverable anomalies, `ERROR` failures needing attention.
- Generate a unique correlation ID at ingress; propagate through logs, spans, and downstream requests (e.g., `X-Correlation-ID`), and return it in the response. `contextvars.ContextVar` and `structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars` support propagation.
- Track latency, traffic, errors, and saturation at every service boundary. Use `prometheus_client.Counter`, `Histogram`, and `Gauge`; instrument requests and operations, and use `time.perf_counter()` for duration.
- Keep metric label values bounded. Unbounded labels (like user IDs) explode storage costs.
- Avoid labels with unbounded values to prevent metric explosion.
- `REQUEST_COUNT.labels(method="GET", user_id=user.id)  # Don't do this!`
- `REQUEST_COUNT.labels(method="GET", endpoint="/users", status="200")` is bounded; bounded sets such as `user_tier="premium"` are appropriate.
- Use OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry.trace`, `TracerProvider`, `BatchSpanProcessor`, `OTLPSpanExporter`) for distributed spans and meaningful attributes. OpenTelemetry evolves; consult https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/ for current API guidance.
- Use reusable timing context managers; keep observability separate from business logic. Test logs and metrics in integration tests and set up alerts.

Never log expected behavior at `ERROR`. A user entering a wrong password is `INFO`, not `ERROR`.
Never use unbounded values as metric labels.
Track the four golden signals - Latency, traffic, errors, saturation.
Log at appropriate levels - Don't cry wolf with ERROR.
